title: East Main: how the day runs
purpose: The flagship's local habits: the morning rush, lunch cover, diagnostics queue, Thursday.
facts: The rush is 7:30 to 10:00; about four cars in ten arrive by 9:00 (mix.json hour curve: 16 % at 7:30 plus 24 % at 8:00).
Since {{@early_desk}} two advisors cover the desk in those hours: one for the counter, one for the phone only (S3: required cover raised from one to two).
Mondays are the worst morning (S3: still 19 % missed).
The foreman hands out work at 7:30.
Diagnostics go to slot 10, about four a day; overflow to slot 18 at Bonny Oaks (S5: eleven orders moved to east during his leave).
Lunch staggered 11:30-13:30; parts land about 9:15, 12:15, 15:15; ready calls by 16:30.
Slot 1 is in on Thursday mornings and his prices do not count.

list_items.section: East Main: how the day runs
list_items.item: Mondays are the worst morning. If you are the phone person on a Monday, you do not leave the desk until 10:00, for anything.

list_items.section: East Main: how the day runs
list_items.item: Randy hands out the work at 7:30 from the day's appointments. A car that was not booked goes to him before you promise it to anyone.

list_items.section: East Main: how the day runs
list_items.item: Diagnostics go to Kevin and he takes about four a day. Book check-engine and electrical jobs into his column, not "any tech". When his column is full it is full: offer the next day, or Bonny Oaks, where Andre takes overflow.

list_items.section: East Main: how the day runs
list_items.item: Lunch is staggered between 11:30 and 1:30. The desk is never empty and the phone is never on voicemail in opening hours.

list_items.section: East Main: how the day runs
list_items.item: Parts runs land about 9:15, 12:15 and 3:15. Call customers about "is my car ready" after a run, not before.

list_items.section: East Main: how the day runs
list_items.item: Ready calls go out by 4:30. After 5:00 people are driving and do not answer.

list_items.section: East Main: how the day runs
list_items.item: Thursday mornings Ray is in the waiting room with a coffee, talking to whoever is there. Customers like it. If he quotes anybody a price, it does not count; he knows.

new_facts: Slot 10 takes about four diagnostic jobs a day. Reason: gives his leave a capacity to be missed; the ERP's diagnostic orders per day at main should fit.
